notes: Her travel journal entries — short reflections on each trip and the books she picked up. Easy to edit/extend without touching code. Order is roughly chronological (oldest at bottom).

entries.body: Visited friends in Manila and rented a car up to Vigan for the weekend. Found the folktales paperback at a tiny bookshop near the cathedral — Sagacious Marcela was on the first page, the king sends her a bird and she sends back a pin. Read it on the bus back, laughed out loud twice.
books: Filipino folktales paperback from a Manila bookshop

entries.body: Mom flew out for my birthday. We took the seabus to Lonsdale and drove up to Cypress to catch the sun on the Lions. I'd just finished re-reading Pauline Johnson's *Legends of Vancouver* — picked up the paperback at the Granville Island bookshop the week before. The Squamish name for the peaks is Ch'ích'iyúy Elx̱wíḵn — the Twin Sisters.
books: Pauline Johnson's Legends of Vancouver from a Granville Island bookshop

entries.body: Six days driving from Vancouver. The light up there does something to you — it stays soft for hours. I bought Service's Yukon ballads at a used bookshop on Main Street and read 'Sam McGee' out loud to the dog at our cabin. Picked up a Jack London paperback at the same shop. To Build a Fire is the most terrifying short story I've ever read about being cold.
books: Service's Yukon ballads (same paperback as the other two)
Jack London paperback from a Whitehorse bookshop

entries.body: Long weekend with C. The whole island smells like the sea. Found a copy of L.M. Montgomery's *Chronicles of Avonlea* at a bookshop downtown — read 'The Quarantine at Alexander Abraham's' on the porch. I have never laughed harder at a story about smallpox.
books: L.M. Montgomery paperback from a Charlottetown bookshop

entries.body: Stopover on the way back east. Stayed in Cabbagetown, found Leacock's *Sunshine Sketches* in a used bookshop on Queen West. The Marine Excursion of the Knights of Pythias is the funniest thing he wrote, even funnier when you've actually been on a small-town Ontario lake at sunset.
books: Leacock paperback from a Toronto bookshop

entries.body: Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen with K — half the day haggling, half the day eating. Picked up a Maupassant paperback for €3. Read 'The Necklace' on the train back to the apartment. The twist ending hit harder when I was tired and a little drunk.
books: Maupassant paperback from a Paris flea market

entries.body: A week in Dublin, mostly walking. Found Wilde at three different bookshops and bought two — the slim Dover edition with 'The Nightingale and the Rose,' and a beautiful hardback of his fairytales for the shelf. The Selfish Giant is the one that actually undoes me. Sat in St. Stephen's Green and read it twice.
books: Wilde paperback from a Dublin bookshop
Wilde fairytales hardback from a Dublin bookshop

entries.body: Bus from London. Stayed in a tiny B&B with sheep visible from the window. The Cotswolds bookshop in Stow had a Saki collection front-of-store — bought it for the train back. 'The Open Window' is the cleverest 6 pages in the language. The whole story is a teenager improvising a ghost story to mess with a houseguest.
books: Saki paperback from a Cotswolds bookshop

entries.body: Three weeks in India. The bookstalls on College Street go on forever. Picked up Tagore's *Mashi and Other Stories* from a man who had to climb a ladder to find a copy in English. Read 'The Postmaster' on a train going north — the lonely civil servant and the orphan girl who loved him in her quiet way. Cried a little.
books: Tagore paperback from a Calcutta bookstall

entries.body: Two weeks across Russia by train. Bought a Chekhov paperback at a kiosk in Moscow — read 'The Bet' twice and still don't know if the lawyer was right. In St. Petersburg I found a thin Tolstoy edition with 'How Much Land Does a Man Need?' Pakhom dies of greed at the end and I haven't stopped thinking about it.
books: Chekhov paperback from a Moscow bookstore

entries.body: First Christmas after the lockdowns. The Strand was packed. I bought an O. Henry paperback with the crooked spine because I felt bad putting it back. 'The Gift of the Magi' on the subway home — the couple sells what they love most to buy each other useless presents. The Times Square Christmas tree was ugly and perfect.
books: O. Henry paperback from a New York used bookstore

entries.body: Leaf-peeping with mom. We stayed at a cabin near Stowe. The bookshop in town had a slim Frost edition with the original woodcut illustrations — bought it without thinking. 'Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening' is the most cozy poem in English. I keep the book on the nightstand for nights I can't sleep.
books: Robert Frost paperback from a Vermont bookshop

entries.body: Long bus ride out to Amherst to see Emily Dickinson's house. Tiny rooms. White dress in a glass case. Bought a slim collection of her poems at the Boston bookshop on the way home. *Hope is the thing with feathers* is the line everyone knows. Reading the others is what makes you understand why.
books: Dickinson poems paperback from a Boston bookshop

entries.body: Bus from Dublin out west. Yeats country. Found a slim collection of his poems at a bookshop in Sligo town. *The Lake Isle of Innisfree* — he wrote it homesick in London, dreaming of a cabin and bean-rows. I have wanted to live alone in a cabin for as long as I can remember.
books: Yeats poetry collection from a Dublin bookshop
